My TOP THREE 3D modelling tips for #gamedev beginners: 1. Turn the model. A LOT. (Every 20 seconds or so you should be turning the camera to be taking ALL angles into account while creating.) Whenever you see a wonky model, eight times out of ten, it is because someone modeled from just the front and side for too long. 2. Work in context. Whenever you can, to maintain a consistent look, model alongside your other models to keep your style the same and to keep scale in mind. Place a character model (even a test one) in your scene as soon as you can for reference on sizing. 3. It's not done until it's in the game. Don't consider something complete until you've put it into your game engine and have seen as it will be seen by the player. So many things change from 3D software to game software... materials, lighting, rendering. You don't want a surprise down the road with work you THOUGHT was complete and then you find out it still needs work in its final form. :)
